19110-the-arena-volume-4-no-19-june-1891.creator: Unknown
19110-the-arena-volume-4-no-19-june-1891.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. History repeats itself, but on new planes. Often, a symbol appears in one age, and the spirit of which it is the expression is revealed in another. Each answers the need of its own time. From the creative standpoint, which is out of time, spirit and symbol are one; but to us, who see things successively, they seem as prior and posterior.

arxiv-1707-03341.title: Use of Docker for deployment and testing of astronomy software Journal: Astronomy & Computing
arxiv-1707-03341.creator: D. Morris, S. Voutsinas, N.C. Hambly and R.G. Mann
arxiv-1707-03341.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by D. Morris, S. Voutsinas, N.C. Hambly and R.G. Mann. We describe preliminary investigations of using Docker for the deployment and testing of astronomy software. Docker is a relatively new containerisation technology that is developing rapidly and being adopted across a range of domains. It is based upon virtualization at operating system level, which presents many advantages in comparison to the more traditional hardware virtualization that underpins most cloud computing infrastructure today.

arxiv-2110-02103.title: Notarial timestamps savings in logs management via Merkle trees and Key Derivation Functions
arxiv-2110-02103.creator: Andrea Barontini
arxiv-2110-02103.description: Abstract Nowadays log files handling imposes to ISPs (intended in their widest scope) strict normative duties apart from common technological issues. This work analyses how retention time policies and timestamping are deeply interlinked from the point of view of service providers, possibly leading to costs rise.

arxiv-2202-01016.title: Nuclear matter in 1 + 1 1+1 dimensions
arxiv-2202-01016.creator: Robert M. Konik, Marton Lajer, Robert D. Pisarski, Alexei M. Tsvelik
arxiv-2202-01016.description: Abstract We review the solution of QCD in two spacetime dimensions. Following the analysis of Baluni, for a single flavor the model can be analyzed using Abelian bosonization. The theory can be analyzed in strong coupling, when the quarks are much lighter than the gauge coupling. In this limit, the theory is given by a Luttinger liquid.

arxiv-2210-14929.title: Investigating Higgs self-interaction through di-Higgs plus jet production
arxiv-2210-14929.creator: Kangyu Chai, Jiang-Hao Yu, Hao Zhang
arxiv-2210-14929.description: Abstract The Higgs self coupling measurement is quite essential for determining the shape of the Higgs potential and nature of the Higgs boson. We propose the di-Higgs plus jet final states at hadron colliders to increase the discovery sensitivity of the Higgs self coupling at the low invariant mass region.

arxiv-2506-15061.title: An Atomic Cluster Expansion Potential for Twisted Multilayer Graphene
arxiv-2506-15061.creator: Yangshuai Wang, Drake Clark, Sambit Das, Ziyan Zhu, Daniel Massatt, Vikram Gavini, Mitchell Luskin, Christoph Ortner
arxiv-2506-15061.description: Abstract Twisted multilayer graphene, characterized by its moiré patterns arising from inter-layer rotational misalignment, serves as a rich platform for exploring quantum phenomena. While first-principles calculations are computationally prohibitive and empirical interatomic potentials often lack accuracy, machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) present a promising alternative, offering (near-)DFT accuracy at a significantly reduced computational cost.

arxiv-2507-19503.title: Fibonacci-harmonic sums
arxiv-2507-19503.description: Abstract We offer several new summation identities involving harmonic numbers, odd harmonic numbers, and Fibonacci numbers. Our results are derived using three different approaches: partial summation, polynomial identities and binomial transformation. arxiv-2509-07191.title: Isospin symmetry breaking and gluon anomaly
arxiv-2509-07191.creator: A. A. Osipov
arxiv-2509-07191.description: Abstract Isospin violating effects, both due to the nonvanishing quark mass difference m d − m u m_{d}-m_{u} and to virtual photons, are studied by fitting the squared masses of pseudoscalar mesons to the second order in the simultaneous expansion in powers of 1 / N c 1/N_{c} , momenta and quark masses.

arxiv-2509-22293.title: EFT of Non-Markovian U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} Breaking: Dark Matter and Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2509-22293.creator: Arnab Chaudhuri
arxiv-2509-22293.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arnab Chaudhuri. We develop an effective field theory (EFT) framework for U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} gauge symmetry breaking in which the dynamics of the order parameter acquire non-local-in-time (“memory”) corrections from a heavy dark sector. Integrating out metastable or slowly equilibrating fields generates temporal kernels in the EFT, yielding a history-dependent effective potential for the U ​ ( 1 ) X U(1)_{X} scalar.

arxiv-2509-25627.title: Casimir effect between semitransparent mirrors in a Lorentz-violating background
arxiv-2509-25627.creator: Román Linares, C. A. Escobar, A. Martín-Ruiz, E. Plácido
arxiv-2509-25627.description: Abstract We investigate the Casimir effect for a massless scalar field confined between two parallel semitransparent mirrors in a vacuum modified by spontaneous Lorentz symmetry breaking. Using Green’s function techniques and a point-splitting evaluation of the stress-energy tensor, we compute the vacuum expectation value of the energy density T 00 T_{00} .

arxiv-2601-03400.title: Eye-Q : A Multilingual Benchmark for Visual Word Puzzle Solving and Image-to-Phrase Reasoning
arxiv-2601-03400.creator: Ali Najar, Alireza Mirrokni, Arshia Izadyari, Sadegh Mohammadian, Amir Homayoon Sharifizade, Asal Meskin, Mobin Bagherian, Ehsaneddin Asgari
arxiv-2601-03400.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Ali Najar, Alireza Mirrokni, Arshia Izadyari, Sadegh Mohammadian, Amir Homayoon Sharifizade, Asal Meskin, Mobin Bagherian, Ehsaneddin Asgari. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on standard vision–language benchmarks, yet often rely on surface-level recognition rather than deeper reasoning. We propose visual word puzzles as a challenging alternative, as they require discovering implicit visual cues, generating and revising hypotheses, and mapping perceptual evidence to non-literal concepts in ways that are difficult to solve via literal grounding, OCR-heavy shortcuts, or simple retrieval-style matching.

pmc-12418676.creator: Margaret Sunitha Selvaraj, Xihao Li, Zilin Li, Eric Van Buren, Sara Haidermota, Darina Postupaka, Whitney Hornsby, Joshua C Bis, Jennifer A Brody, Brian E Cade, Ren-Hua Chung, Joanne E Curran, Scott M Damrauer, Lisa de las Fuentes, Paul S de Vries, Ravindranath Duggirala, Barry I Freedman, MariaElis

pmc-12692364.title: The Impact of Smartphone Addiction on PTSD Symptoms Among South African University Students: Resilience as a Protective Factor
pmc-12692364.creator: Anita Padmanabhanunni, Tyrone B Pretorius, César Leal-Costa
pmc-12692364.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Problematic smartphone use was significantly associated with higher levels of post-traumatic stress symptoms among South African university students.Resilience moderated this relationship, buffering the impact of smartphone addiction on PTSD symptoms and reducing psychological distress among individuals with higher resilience.

pmc-12766319.title: Drug Repurposing as an Effective Drug Discovery Strategy: A Critical Review
pmc-12766319.creator: Abdulaziz H Al Khzem, Saad M Wali
pmc-12766319.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Drug repurposing, or repositioning, has emerged as a pivotal strategy in pharmaceutical research, offering a promising approach to uncover new therapeutic uses for existing drugs. While traditional de novo drug discovery typically requires 10–17 years and investments exceeding $2 billion with only 11% of Phase I candidates reaching approval, drug repurposing can reduce development timelines to 3–12 years at substantially lower costs, with approval rates reaching approximately 30% for de-risked compounds.

pmc-13302899.title: Dose Adjustment of JAK Inhibitors for the Management of Moderate-to-Severe Atopic Dermatitis: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study
pmc-13302899.creator: Costanza Falcidia, Francesco D’Oria, Giulio Foggi, Paola Facheris, Matteo Bianco, Luciano Ibba, Alessandra Narcisi, Antonio Costanzo, Luigi Gargiulo
pmc-13302899.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and Objectives: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors have expanded the therapeutic options for moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD). The possibility of dose modulation with abrocitinib (100 and 200 mg) and upadacitinib (15 and 30 mg), both selective JAK1 inhibitors, represents a potential clinical advantage, allowing dose escalation in cases of insufficient response and dose de-escalation in the setting of poor tolerability or during maintenance treatment. However, real-world data remain limited, and the rationale for dose adjustment is not always standardized.
